subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Two Collectors That Removed 94%, Not 150%
featured_title: THE TWO COLLECTORS THAT REMOVED 94 PERCENT, NOT 150

presentation.challenge: A 70% cyclone followed by an 80% baghouse did not provide 150% removal. The second device treated only what escaped the first, giving 94% overall removal.

practice.primary_question: How are particulate-control efficiencies combined when two collection devices operate in series?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Adding the efficiencies of two control devices in series instead of multiplying the fractions that remain after each stage.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 70% cyclone and 80% baghouse give 150% overall particulate removal.
case_dna.why_plausible: Both values are removal percentages, so direct addition is tempting even though the second device sees only the mass that escapes the first.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: From 100 kg/hr inlet, 30 kg/hr leaves the cyclone. The baghouse removes 80% of 30=24 kg/hr, leaving 6 kg/hr. Overall removal is 94%.
case_dna.corrected_model: For independent series devices, the overall fraction remaining is the product of the stage fractions remaining: (1-η1)(1-η2).

problem_statement: A particulate stream of 100 kg/hr enters a cyclone with 70% collection efficiency, followed by a baghouse with 80% collection efficiency based on the particulate entering the baghouse. A note adds the efficiencies and reports 150% removal. Determine the outlet particulate rate and overall collection efficiency.
fixed_constraints: Baghouse efficiency=80% of its inlet particulate

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The second collector did not receive the original 100 kg/hr.
facts: Baghouse removes 80% of what reaches it
gates.prompt: What particulate rate reaches the baghouse?
gates.cta: Track the fraction remaining after the cyclone

options.label: Use fraction remaining=(1-η1)(1-η2)
options.reason: Each device acts on the particulate that survives the previous stage.

options.label: Use ηoverall=η1+η2
options.reason: Adding stage efficiencies double-counts material and can exceed 100%.

options.label: Use the arithmetic mean of the efficiencies
options.reason: A simple average does not represent the series mass balance.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the final particulate rate
gates.prompt: Enter the outlet particulate rate in kg/hr.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Track particulate through both collectors
gates.result: Only 6 kg/hr remains after both devices.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the overall collection
gates.hint: Multiply the two fractions that remain: 0.30×0.20.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Each stage acts on a smaller remaining mass

cards.text: The baghouse removes 0.80×30=24 kg/hr, leaving 6 kg/hr.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the series-control note
report: C2. Baghouse efficiency is 80% of its inlet particulate.
C3. Therefore total collection efficiency is 70%+80%=150%.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated cyclone efficiency.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated baghouse efficiency basis.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Series efficiencies cannot be added because the second stage treats only the first-stage remainder.

evidence_choices.reason: This correctly combines the fractions remaining after each device.

correction.template: The outlet is {outlet} kg/hr and the overall particulate collection efficiency is {overall_efficiency}%.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reach 98% overall collection with the same cyclone

options.label: Use a second-stage efficiency of at least 93.3%
Use a 28% second-stage device
options.reason: That leaves too much particulate after the second stage.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Combine another pair of series collectors
gates.prompt: What is the overall efficiency of a 60% device followed by a 90% device?

options.reason: The arithmetic mean does not represent the series mass balance.

gates.explanation: Multiply the fractions that remain, then subtract from one.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the particle-control calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that series collection efficiencies combine through the fractions remaining after each device, not by direct addition.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Two collection percentages were added directly.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The baghouse receives only the particulate that escapes the cyclone.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use ηoverall=1-(1-η1)(1-η2) for the stated two-stage series system.

seo.seo_title: Series Particle Control Efficiency | FE Environmental E-076
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-076: a 70% cyclone followed by an 80% baghouse removes 94% overall, leaving 6 kg/hr from a 100 kg/hr inlet.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental series particle control efficiency
seo.excerpt: Control-device efficiencies in series do not add. Track the fraction remaining after each collection stage.
seo.direct_answer: The cyclone leaves 100(1-0.70)=30 kg/hr. The baghouse leaves 30(1-0.80)=6 kg/hr. Overall collection is 1-6/100=94%.
